changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 6 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6594-headercolor-mirror-enum.md`

- names `packages/types/src/views.ts` → `packages/types/src/views.ts` — edited by this change

  > The nearest precedent is objectui#5853 (`.changeset/5853-tablecolumn-type-canonical-union.md`), which narrowed `TableColumn.type` on the same three-ends pattern and **exported** a `TABLE_COLUMN_TYPES` tuple for the zod mirror to build its enum from. That shape is not available here and the difference is structural, not a preference: `packages/types/src/views.ts` is a **type-only** module, so a tuple there would add a runtime export to the package barrel (a value export cannot ride the barrel's `export type` block) and a runtime import edge from the zod entry into `views.js`. #5853 had a second reason to export — producers needed its `normalizeTableColumnType()` at their emit seam — and `headerColor` has no producer that needs a runtime value. The literals are therefore written on each half and the anti-drift guarantee is carried by the pin above, which also covers the third end a shared tuple could not reach: the renderer, in a package `@object-ui/types` must not depend on.

### `.changeset/7287-resolve-title-field-shared-ladder.md`

- names `views.ts` → `packages/types/src/views.ts` — edited by this change

  > `def.primaryField` — a `DetailViewSchema` key (`@object-ui/types` `views.ts`), read off an OBJECT def and ranked ABOVE the canonical `nameField` ADR-0079 Phase 2 made the pointer (AGENTS.md Commandment #0.1). No producer can put it there: `@objectstack/spec`'s object schema is a `strictObject` that answers `unrecognized_keys: ['primaryField']`, and `ObjectSchema.create()` throws — which is why objectstack#6326 deleted the identical read from two lint rules. A census across both repos found **zero** object payloads carrying it (the only writers are three test fixtures), and `primaryField` appears in **zero** files of the shipped `@objectstack/spec@17.2.0` dist against 68 for `nameField`. Same shape as the undeclared `objectDef.titleField` read objectui#6531 measured and #6557 removed. `DetailViewSchema.primaryField` is untouched and still honoured by `DetailView`'s own header — it is a view key, and on a view it is legitimate.

### `.changeset/7344-handler-string-any-mirrors.md`

- names `views.zod.ts` → `packages/types/src/zod/views.zod.ts` — edited by this change

  > The three `views.zod.ts` `z.string()` keys that are event NAMES (`onViewChange`, the two `onChange`, PR #6899) are untouched; their describe text says so and the new pin reads it. `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` records the three new runtime-slot drift rows; `content/docs/core/app-schema.mdx` spells its `AppAction.onClick` row `never` and drops the string example, the two edits the #7340 docs pin and `check:doc-snippets` require.

### `.changeset/7586-primary-field-consumer-reads.md`

- names `views.ts` → `packages/types/src/views.ts` — edited by this change

  > `primaryField` is a `DetailViewSchema` key (`@object-ui/types` `views.ts`) — a **view** key, which `DetailView.resolveDisplayTitle` reads off `schema` and is welcome to. Read off an **object** def it is undeclared: `@objectstack/spec`'s object schema is a `strictObject` answering `unrecognized_keys: ['primaryField']`, and `ObjectSchema.create()` throws. `primaryField` appears in **zero** files of the shipped `@objectstack/spec@17.2.0` dist, against 68 for the canonical `nameField`. objectstack#6326 removed the identical read from two lint rules; objectui#7287 / PR #7585 removed it from `resolveTitleField`. These two survived it — and three of this repo's own changelogs already called the probe *"not a spec property — always undefined"* while the code kept honouring it.

### `.changeset/7735-zod-mirrors-stop-authoring-defaults.md`

- names `views.zod.ts` → `packages/types/src/zod/views.zod.ts` — edited by this change

  > **What changed.** All 41 `.default()` call sites under `packages/types/src/zod/` are removed — `layout.zod.ts` 22, `crud.zod.ts` 11, `form.zod.ts` 5, `views.zod.ts` 2, `app.zod.ts` 1. `@object-ui/components` reconciles the third face objectui#8229 found: `flex`'s registration `defaultProps.align` seeded `'center'`, the value its own renderer never applies, so a designer-made node laid out differently from a hand-authored one; it now seeds `'start'`.

### `.changeset/9511-record-id-is-a-string.md`

- names `views.ts` → `packages/types/src/views.ts` — edited by this change

  > **The three authorable keys, each on BOTH faces.** `ObjectFormSchema.recordId` (`objectql.ts` + `zod/objectql.zod.ts`), `DetailViewSchema.resourceId` (`views.ts` + `zod/views.zod.ts`) and `DetailSchema.resourceId` (`crud.ts` + `zod/crud.zod.ts`). ⚠️ The `crud` pair is **`DetailSchema`**, not `DetailViewSchema`, and it reaches the same renderer — not by symbol but by data flow: `plugin-detail` registers the `'detail'` node type onto `DetailView`. A read that follows TypeScript symbols alone finds two keys and is incomplete.

- names `zod/views.zod.ts` → `packages/types/src/zod/views.zod.ts` — edited by this change

  > **The three authorable keys, each on BOTH faces.** `ObjectFormSchema.recordId` (`objectql.ts` + `zod/objectql.zod.ts`), `DetailViewSchema.resourceId` (`views.ts` + `zod/views.zod.ts`) and `DetailSchema.resourceId` (`crud.ts` + `zod/crud.zod.ts`). ⚠️ The `crud` pair is **`DetailSchema`**, not `DetailViewSchema`, and it reaches the same renderer — not by symbol but by data flow: `plugin-detail` registers the `'detail'` node type onto `DetailView`. A read that follows TypeScript symbols alone finds two keys and is incomplete.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `0896838de` (merge-base with origin/main): 4 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1576 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2164 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36303574820)

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e0fdfb5647ed51ed65d51e0bc6b5aec454379e71`

### ① Derived judgments

- **Refusal at the door.** `objectui validate` and `objectui check` call `safeValidateSchema` (`packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts`, `check.ts`), which is `AnyComponentSchema.safeParse`; the `filter-ui` literal selects `FilterUISchema`, whose `filters[]` element now carries `retirementTombstone(guidance)` = `z.never({ error: guidance }).optional().describe(guidance)`. Probe on zod 4.4.3 (the pinned version): `operator` set to `gt`, `greater_than` or `zz_nonsense_op` is refused as exactly one issue `{ code: 'invalid_type', path: ['filters', 1, 'operator'] }` with `message === description`. The message names the card, why nothing reads the key, and the remedy (remove it). The pin's block (a) asserts the same envelope at both doors; the pin matches the CI `unit` include (`packages/**/*.test.ts`) and all eight Test shards are green.
- **Strip vs tombstone.** The element is `z.array(z.object({...}))`, not `.passthrough()` and not strict; probe: a misspelled `operatr` parses green and is gone after parse (keys `['field','type']`). So a plain deletion would have been a silent accept; the tombstone is the right form, consistent with the `body` / `children` tombstones already on the same schema and with the helper's own docblock.
- **Producer / reader census (re-derived, lit controls).** `FilterUI.tsx` reads entries by name only (`type`, `field`, `label`, `placeholder`, `options`); there is no `...filter` or `...schema` spread, and `operator` lives on an array element, so the `SchemaRenderer` node-key spread cannot carry it separately. `grep operator` in `packages/plugin-view/src` hits only view-filter rules (`{ field, operator, value }` on named views / `FilterBuilder`), a different vocabulary. Every in-repo `filter-ui` author (catalog `filter-ui.json`, registration `defaultProps` and `inputs`, `phase2-schemas`, `RecordPickerDialog` bridge whose columns are `field/label/type/options`, expression-carriage fixture, docs) writes no `operator`. objectstack `origin/main` `e2c4e125`: `filter-ui` 0 files, control `object-grid` 56; `FilterUISchema` 0 hits. No producer, no reader; the stop condition did not fire.
- **Docs.** The Schema block now lists `field / label? / type / options? / placeholder?`, all true to the TS face. The "Retired" prose is true: the renderer emits via `notifyViewHandlerChannels(onChange, schema.onChange, nextValues, { values })`, and the key is refused when validated.
- **Pin can fail; ablations cohere.** 16 tests = 9 `it.each` + 2 + 2 + 1 + 2. Mirror reverted to the enum ⇒ 9 refusals fail, the one-string test throws on `issuesOf(r)[0]`, "stays DECLARED" passes ⇒ 10/6 as claimed. TS reverted ⇒ `TS2344` on `assertionOperatorRetired`, `TS2578` on the unused directive, parity `TS2322` on `views.zod.ts#FilterUISchema` (the ratchet row exists) all follow. Cross-package `TS2322 string → undefined` is the expected widened message.
- **Scope.** Five files, all inside the claim's file surface; `FilterUI.tsx` untouched. All 43 check runs are `success` or path-skipped; every required context (Lint, Type Check, Build & E2E, Build Docs, Changeset Declaration, Test, Spec Main Shape Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard) is `success`. Merge base `1422a920ed` as the PR body states.
- **Defect (blocking, prose).** Changeset line "so `operator: 'gt'`, or a nonsense id, type-checked, parsed green through `objectui validate`" is born false for the nonsense id: the pre-change mirror was `z.enum([...])` and the TS member the same union, so `zz_nonsense_op` / `greater_than` were refused (`invalid_value`, probe above) and did not type-check; only the render reading was identical. The same false clause is in the pin header ("type-checked, parsed green"). The `views.ts` docblock ("rendered and emitted exactly what a filter without it does") is the true form.
- Nit, non-blocking: "emits `{ values }` only (to a host `onChange` function and to the authored window event)" — the host function receives the bare record; only the window `detail` is `{ values }`. Substance (no operator anywhere) holds.

### ② Semver level

`minor` for `@object-ui/types` with a BREAKING banner, `major` refused per the version-alignment rule; `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Declaration` and `Changeset Fixed Group Check` all green. Every other changeset sentence is true (seven-member enum, plain object strips, `invalid_type` at `filters.N.operator`, no replacement key, one-time census recorded on the PR, pin path exists). The one false clause is the "nonsense id … type-checked, parsed green" sentence above; because a changeset publishes verbatim into the CHANGELOG and published CHANGELOG paragraphs are never re-addressed, it is listed as blocking.

### ③ Boundary flags

- (a) The model-named `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5` trailer cannot reach `main`. Ruleset `main`: `merge_queue.merge_method = SQUASH`; repo settings `squash_merge_commit_title = PR_TITLE`, `squash_merge_commit_message = PR_BODY`; the PR body carries no model name. Empirical control: PR #10733's four commits all carried that exact trailer and its squash `7b395d8c56` on `main` carries only the author-derived `Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` that GitHub appends to every squash here; a grep of the last 300 `main` commits finds zero model-named trailers. The trailer survives only in the PR's own commit, which the branch deletion after merge retires.
- (b) `multi-select` missing from the docs `type` union pre-exists on `main` (docs line lacks it, `views.ts` has it) and is outside the card, so deferring it was correct; it under-teaches and invites no wrong metadata. But "carrier: none" means nothing owns it now — the PM seat should file a docs card or it is lost.
- Other: the PR is correctly still draft (dispatched-PR rule ②); NOT GOVERNED paths; `Fixes #10611` closes only the intended card.
